units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 85">Gen. R. s. 85</cite>, beg. <he>שָׁקַרְתָּ יהודה</he> thou hast been false, O Judah; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 144">Yalk. ib. 144</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 589">Yalk. Mal. 589</cite>.

senses.gloss: same, to lie; to defraud.—מה לי לשַׁקּר what reason should I have for making a false statement?, i.e. a person’s statement is to be credited, when he gains nothing by it, since he might have obtained the same advantage in another way.
units: <cite ref="Kiddushin 64b:1">Kidd. 64ᵇ</cite> <he>אמרינן מה לי לשקר וכ׳</he> we apply the principle that we believe him, because he gains nothing by falsehood: for, why should he have said so? In order to release her from leviratical marriage after his death? If so, he might have said to her: I release thee by a divorce.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 64b:2">Ib.</cite> <he>מה לי לש׳ כי עדים דמי</he> a person’s statement accepted on the ground that he had no reason for lying, has the same legal value as the statement of witnesses; <he>מה לי לש׳ כי חזקה דמי</he> it has only the same value as a presumption (<cite ref="H00556"><he>חֲזָקָה</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Ketubot 27b:3">Keth. 27ᵇ</cite> <he>מה לי לש׳ אי בעי וכ׳</he> we must believe him, for, if he had wanted, he might have said &c.

Ib. מה לי לש׳ במקום עדים וכ׳ we do not apply the principle of mah li l’shaḳḳer, when the person’s statement is contradicted by witnesses (by well-known facts); B. Mets. 81ᵇ; a. fr.—Y. Snh. XI, 30ᶜ top (expl. כחש לו, I Kings XIII, 18) שי׳ בו (not ביה) he played him false; Cant. R. to II, 5 שי׳ לו; ib. ומה שי׳ לו שהאכילהו וכ׳ and wherein did he play him false? In that he gave him the bread of deceit to eat (made him the recipient of treacherous hospitality).
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 20:19">Num. R. s. 20<sup>18</sup></cite>; Tanḥ. Balak 12 <he>מְשַׁקֵּר במשקלות</he>, v. <cite ref="M02966"><he>מִשְׁקָל</he></cite>; a. fr.

<cite ref="Makkot 5a:8">Macc. 5ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 19:18">Deut. XIX, 18</cite>) <he>עד שתְּשַׁקֵּר גופה וכ׳</he> until thou disprovest the body of the testimony (provest an alibi of the witnesses).

senses.gloss: to be refuted, be proved to be a liar. Y. ib. I, beg. 31ᵃ [read:] עדים שנזדממו וחזרו ונִשְׁתַּקְּרוּ if witnesses against whom an alibi had been proved were also proved to have told a falsehood (as to the fact to which they testified).
